messages.subject: [statnet_help] AIC and BIC from package:ergm.ego
messages.body_plain:
To the Statnet team,

I have been fitting ERGMs with package:ergm.ego and would now like to do some formal, data driven model selection using AIC or BIC.

I am aware that this is calculated within package:ergm, but is this the case for package:ergm.ego?

If not, can this be simply calculated from the log likelihood (`model$loglikelihood`) as per convention? (e.g. AIC = ? 2 ? ln likelihood +2 k +1), or is this an oversimplification?

Many thanks and best wishes,

Will

messages.subject: [statnet_help] AIC and BIC from package:ergm.ego
messages.body_plain:
Dear William,

ergm.ego's inference is not, strictly speaking, likelihood-based (see Krivitsky and Morris, 2017), so it doesn't report AIC, BIC, or other likelihood-based quantities.

I hope this helps,
Pavel

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Comparing homophily for select groups
messages.body_plain:
Hi-

I have a network directed, non-valued (0/1) ties and a node attribute, ethnicity. I want to use ERGM to compare the propensities of two ethic groups, A and B, to send ties to ethnicity C. In other words, I want to know if members of group A are more likely than members of group B to send ties to C.

How should I go about it?

Best,
Denis


Denis Trapido
Associate Professor
Management and Organization
School of Business
University of Washington Bothell
